subject: Hosted API: sudden p99 latency surge tied to batching queueing
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha@novasys.com>
To: support@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ops@novasys.com
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 22:16:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden p99 spike affecting critical flows

Hi team,

We started seeing a major p99 latency spike on the Hosted API around 21:45 PST. Our platform (Novasys) runs a bursty inference workload for realtime recommendations; p95 elevated slightly but p99 is spiking to 6-8s which is breaking our SLAs and causing request timeouts in our edge services. This looks correlated with larger request batching on your side — our observability shows a sharp increase in request queue depth around the same time.

Attached is a short slowlog sample (novasys-slowlog-2027-11-21.txt) and a link to our internal error traces. Can your ops team confirm whether there was a scheduling/regression or a batching policy change? We need an ETA for mitigation — this is impacting a paying production customer.

Thanks,
Asha Patel
Head of Platform, Novasys
asha@novasys.com

Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike affecting critical flows

Lauren / team — initial findings:
- No recent config commits to batching policy in prod; autoscaler shows two back-to-back scale events at 21:37 and 21:42 (scale-up), followed by a transient scheduling delay for several containers due to node provisioning lag in us-west-2.
- The runtime switched to a larger coalesced-batching kernel for the Novasys model at 21:33 because of aggregated sequence-length signal; that change increased average batch assembly time by ~30ms but created a tail when node provisioning delayed consumption.
- Queue depth histograms show a heavy tail between 21:40–22:00 with incremental retries from the client exacerbating buildup.

Immediate mitigations applied at 07:20 PST:
- Forced fallback to the previous kernel that prioritizes latency (rolling)
- Temporarily reduced maximum batching window for the affected shard from 25ms to 12ms
- Throttled non-essential background traffic to free capacity

Preliminary impact: p99 dropped from ~7.8s down to ~1.2s on sampled traffic; p95 near baseline.

Next steps: full postmortem and tuning recommendations for adaptive batching to avoid similar tail-behavior during provisioning events. Adding notes to INF-4721.

Marissa
Sr. Prod Ops, Redwood Inference

Asha — quick update and suggested short-term mitigations:

What happened: provisioning lag in us-west-2 caused a transient consumption bottleneck. The runtime’s adaptive kernel choice increased batch assembly times during that window which amplified tail latency; client retries then compounded queue depth. No code regressions were deployed to production — this was an operational interaction between autoscaler timing and kernel switching heuristic.

Short-term guidance for Novasys:
- Reduce aggressive client-side retry attempts for 502/timeout responses; implement exponential backoff with jitter (suggest starting at 250ms base).
- Consider temporary per-route concurrency limits on your side to smooth bursty fan-in.
- We'll provide a minimal client-side snippet and policy doc in the shared Drive link.

Longer-term actions we will take:
- Ship an adaptive batching guard that detects provisioning stalls and forces low-latency kernel / reduces batching window automatically (tracking INF-4721).
- Improve autoscaler instrumentation and capacity warm pools to avoid node provisioning tail.
- Postmortem with timeline, RCA, and regression tests for kernel selection logic.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync with your ops at 11:15 PST to walk the mitigation steps and share the mitigation-plan-draft.pdf. Thanks for the patience and flagging this quickly — we'll follow up with a full RCA in 48 hours.

Regards,
